'''Richard Furneaux''' is a New Zealand carbohydrate chemist. He is known for leadership in chemistry and research commercialisation, and his role as the first director of the [[Ferrier Research Institute]]. He is currently director of Humblebee Ltd.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Discovery |url=https://people.wgtn.ac.nz/richard.furneaux/professional |access-date=2026-01-18 |website=people.wgtn.ac.nz}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Furneaux completed his PhD at [[Victoria University of Wellington]], under the supervision of [[Robin Ferrier]]. He then completed a postdoctoral fellowship in the lab of Fred Shafizadeh at the [[University of Montana]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-09-30 |title=Professor Richard H Furneaux – ACOLA |url=https://acola.org/richard-furneaux/ |access-date=2026-01-18 |language=en-US}}</ref> Following his fellowship, he returned to New Zealand and worked at [[Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (New Zealand)|Department of Scientific and Industrial Research]]. He eventually leading the carbohydrate team in what became [[Industrial Research Limited]] and eventually the [[Ferrier Research Institute]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-01-17 |title=GlycoSyn 'bringing home the bacon' in science commercialisation |url=https://www.nbr.co.nz/tech/glycosyn-bringing-home-the-bacon-in-science-commercialisation/ |access-date=2026-01-18 |website=NBR {{!}} Business news & analysis {{!}} Independent, ad-free reporting |language=en-NZ}}</ref>

In collaboration with [[Vern L. Schramm]], Furneaux and [[Peter Tyler]] designed and synthesised [[Forodesine]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Victoria University of Wellington. Faculty of Science. School of Geography |first=Environment and Earth Sciences |date=2017-04-19 |title=Victoria research leads to new drug for hard-to-treat lymphomas {{!}} Te Wāhanga Pūtaiao / Faculty of Science {{!}} Te Herenga Waka |url=https://www.wgtn.ac.nz/science/about/news/news-archives/2017-news/victoria-research-leads-to-new-drug-for-hard-to-treat-lymphomas |access-date=2026-01-18 |website=Victoria University of Wellington |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Stuff |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/science/95090088/national-portrait--richard-furneaux-pioneering-chemist |access-date=2026-01-18 |website=www.stuff.co.nz}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Stuff |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/business/innovation/94806030/cancer-cure-20-years-in-the-making-hits-international-shelves |access-date=2026-01-18 |website=www.stuff.co.nz}}</ref>

Furneaux is a Fellow of the [[Royal Society Te Aparangi]] and was awarded the [[Hector Medal]] in 2006 and Thomson Medal in 2012.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 Hector Medal |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/what-we-do/medals-and-awards/medals-and-awards-news/2012-hector-medal/ |access-date=2026-01-18 |website=Royal Society Te Apārangi}}</ref> He was awarded Wellingtonian of the Year in Science and Technology in 2013 and won the Kiwinet Supreme Award in 2017.
